```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 6, fig.height = 4)
library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
```

# Models and source

Steichert et al. (2025) used the plasma angiotensin II / angiotensin I ratio
as a pharmacodynamic measure of in vivo angiotensin-converting-enzyme (ACE)
activity during enalapril treatment and fitted two independent models in
Monolix 2024R1. Both are packaged here and share this article:

* `Steichert_2025_enalaprilat_angiotensin_adult`: population PK/PD model in
  nine healthy adults after one 20 mg tablet of enalapril maleate (enalaprilat
  PK with transit absorption, an effect compartment and a sigmoid Imax model).
* `Steichert_2025_enalaprilat_angiotensin_pediatric`: population PD model in 27
  ACE-inhibitor-naive children with heart failure from the LENA studies (direct
  Imax model on the measured serum enalaprilat concentration).

```{r load-models}
mod_adult <- readModelDb("Steichert_2025_enalaprilat_angiotensin_adult")
mod_ped <- readModelDb("Steichert_2025_enalaprilat_angiotensin_pediatric")
```

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(mod_adult)$reference`
* Adult model: `r rxode2::rxode(mod_adult)$description`
* Paediatric model: `r rxode2::rxode(mod_ped)$description`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.3390/pharmaceutics17101345>

# Population

**Healthy adults** (Section 2.1, Table 1): nine subjects (6 male, 3 female)
from a single-dose, open-label study at Heinrich Heine University Duesseldorf
in 2013; age 19-30 years (median 21), weight 47-88 kg (median 74), BMI
18-25 kg/m^2. After a fast of at least 10 h each received one 20 mg enalapril
maleate tablet (median 0.27 mg/kg). Serum enalaprilat was sampled densely to
8 h and at 24, 48 and 72 h (288 concentrations, 47 below the 0.70 ug/L LLOQ and
treated as left-censored); angiotensin I and II were sampled predose and at
0.5-8, 24, 48 and 72 h, and the 99 ratios up to 24 h were modelled.

**Children with heart failure** (Sections 2.2 and 3.2, Table 1): 27
ACE-inhibitor-naive children (15 female) from two LENA PK-bridging studies and
their safety follow-up study (Austria, Germany, Hungary, the Netherlands and
Serbia, 2016-2018); 24 had congenital heart disease and 3 dilated
cardiomyopathy. Across the 54 observations, age was 0.07-2.24 years (median
0.36), weight 3.2-13.0 kg (median 4.8) and modified Ross score 0-9 (median 4).
Children received enalapril maleate orodispersible minitablets (median first
dose 0.06 mg/kg). The 54 paired enalaprilat concentration / ratio observations
were 16 before the first dose, 12 after the first dose and 26 after repeated
doses (3.9 days to 11.8 months).

The same information is available programmatically through each model's
`population` metadata.

# Source trace

Every `ini()` value carries an in-file comment naming its source. The table
collects them.

| Model | Parameter / equation | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|---|
| adult | `ktr` | 5.31 1/h | Table 2 |
| adult | `mtt` | 1.46 h | Table 2 |
| adult | `ka` | 1.19 1/h | Table 2 |
| adult | `cl` (CL/F) | 36.39 L/h | Table 2 |
| adult | `vc` (V1/F) | 223.71 L | Table 2 |
| adult | `q` (Q/F) | 6.38 L/h | Table 2 |
| adult | `vp` (V2/F) | 108.26 L | Table 2 |
| adult | `ke0` | 0.48 1/h | Table 2 |
| adult | `hill` (gamma) | 2.02 | Table 2 |
| adult | `e0` | 0.043 | Table 2 |
| adult | `ic50` | 30.01 ug/L | Table 2 |
| adult | IIV ktr, Mtt, CL/F, V1/F, E0, IC50 | 72.89, 33.7, 30.17, 46.61, 141.9, 79.35 CV% | Table 2 |
| adult | Correlation V1/F, CL/F | 0.84 | Table 2 |
| adult | PK residual error | proportional 0.072, additive 0.42 ug/L | Table 2; combined model, Section 3.3.1 |
| adult | PD residual error | proportional 0.41 | Table 2; Section 3.3.1 |
| adult | Transit + first-order absorption, two compartments, linear elimination | -- | Section 3.3.1 |
| adult | Effect compartment `dCe/dt = ke0 (Cc - Ce)` | -- | Sections 2.4.1 and 3.3.1 |
| adult | `E = E0 (1 - Ce^gamma / (Ce^gamma + IC50^gamma))` | -- | Section 3.3.1 (full inhibition with sigmoidicity factor; Monolix library form) |
| paediatric | `e0` | 0.19 | Table 3 |
| paediatric | `ic50` | 1.19 ug/L | Table 3 |
| paediatric | IIV IC50 | 59.92 CV% | Table 3 |
| paediatric | Residual error | proportional 0.37 | Table 3; Section 3.6.1 |
| paediatric | `E = E0 (1 - C / (C + IC50))` | -- | Section 3.6.1 (full inhibition, no sigmoidicity factor) |

The paper prints no model equations; the effect-compartment and Imax forms
above are the standard Monolix library forms named in the text.

# Dose basis: enalapril free base

The enalaprilat model has no enalapril state, so the dose enters as an amount
of enalapril that the absorption compartment converts to enalaprilat. Doses are
entered as enalapril **free base** in ug, the same basis as the group's
paediatric enalapril / enalaprilat PK model
(`Steichert_2025_enalapril_enalaprilat_pediatric`). One 20 mg enalapril maleate
tablet is `20000 * 376.45 / 492.52 = 15287` ug of enalapril base.

Figure 3a plots the population predictions (PRED) of every adult PK sample;
those are the typical-value profile evaluated at the sampling times, so the
right-most PRED column is the typical Cmax. Read from the figure by the
maintainers, it lies at about 46 ug/L. Figure 4a likewise shows the PRED of the
ratio spanning about 0.018 (the typical nadir) to 0.043 (E0). The check below
evaluates the typical profile under three candidate dose amounts.

```{r dose-basis}
MW_ENALAPRIL <- 376.45
MW_ENALAPRILAT <- 348.40
MW_ENALAPRIL_MALEATE <- 492.52
dose_candidates <- c(
  "enalapril base (used)" = 20000 * MW_ENALAPRIL / MW_ENALAPRIL_MALEATE,
  "enalaprilat equivalent" = 20000 * MW_ENALAPRILAT / MW_ENALAPRIL_MALEATE,
  "maleate salt mass" = 20000
)
DOSE_ADULT_UG <- dose_candidates[["enalapril base (used)"]]

mod_adult_typ <- rxode2::zeroRe(mod_adult)
obs_grid <- seq(0, 24, by = 0.05)

# Two declared endpoints: observe on the ODE state with dvid = 1, which
# returns every endpoint column (Cc and ang2_ang1_ratio) at each row.
make_adult_events <- function(ids, dose_ug, times) {
  doses <- data.frame(id = ids, time = 0, evid = 1L, amt = dose_ug, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_)
  obs <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = ids, time = times) |>
    dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = NA_real_, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L)
  dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |> dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))
}

typ_by_dose <- lapply(names(dose_candidates), function(nm) {
  ev <- make_adult_events(1L, dose_candidates[[nm]], obs_grid)
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_adult_typ, ev))
  data.frame(
    dose_basis = nm,
    amt_ug = round(dose_candidates[[nm]]),
    Cmax = max(s$Cc),
    tmax = s$time[which.max(s$Cc)],
    ratio_nadir = min(s$ang2_ang1_ratio)
  )
}) |> dplyr::bind_rows()

typ_by_dose |>
  dplyr::mutate(Cmax = signif(Cmax, 3), ratio_nadir = signif(ratio_nadir, 3)) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Dose basis" = dose_basis, "Amount (ug)" = amt_ug,
    "Typical Cmax (ug/L)" = Cmax, "Typical tmax (h)" = tmax,
    "Typical ratio nadir" = ratio_nadir
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  # Figure 3a right-most PRED column ~46 ug/L.
  abs(typ_by_dose$Cmax[1] / 46 - 1) < 0.05,
  # The salt mass would put the PRED peak near 61 ug/L.
  typ_by_dose$Cmax[3] > 55,
  # Figure 4a left-most PRED column ~0.018.
  abs(typ_by_dose$ratio_nadir[1] / 0.018 - 1) < 0.10
)
```

The base dose reproduces both PRED extremes. The enalaprilat-equivalent dose
(43 ug/L) is close but sits visibly below the figure's PRED maximum, and the
salt mass (61 ug/L) is far off.

# Scale of the random effects

Table 2 and Table 3 report IIV as "CV%". Monolix estimates the standard
deviation omega of each log-normal random effect and reports the coefficient
of variation `sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`, so the models use
`omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`. The alternative reading, `omega = CV / 100`, gives a
very different E0 variance (2.01 instead of 1.10, because the E0 CV is 141.9%).

The predose bin of the PD visual predictive check (Figure 4b) separates the
two. Before the dose, the ratio is `E0 * (1 + 0.41 * eps)`, so its percentiles
depend only on the E0 variance and the residual error. Read by the maintainers
from Figure 4b at time 0, the 90% prediction interval of the 90th percentile
spans about 0.08-0.50, and that of the median about 0.03-0.085. The Monte Carlo
below repeats the VPC for nine subjects, 2000 times, under each reading.

```{r omega-scale}
set.seed(20251025)
omega_e0_used <- rxode2::rxode(mod_adult)$omega["etale0", "etale0"]
vpc_t0 <- function(omega2, n_subj = 9, n_rep = 2000) {
  pct <- t(replicate(n_rep, {
    e0 <- 0.043 * exp(rnorm(n_subj, 0, sqrt(omega2)))
    y <- e0 * (1 + 0.41 * rnorm(n_subj))
    stats::quantile(y, c(0.1, 0.5, 0.9), type = 5)
  }))
  apply(pct, 2, stats::quantile, c(0.05, 0.95))
}
pi_log <- vpc_t0(omega_e0_used)
pi_sd <- vpc_t0(1.419^2)

data.frame(
  reading = c("omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2) (used)", "omega = CV / 100"),
  omega2_E0 = signif(c(omega_e0_used, 1.419^2), 3),
  p50_PI = c(sprintf("%.3f-%.3f", pi_log[1, 2], pi_log[2, 2]), sprintf("%.3f-%.3f", pi_sd[1, 2], pi_sd[2, 2])),
  p90_PI = c(sprintf("%.3f-%.3f", pi_log[1, 3], pi_log[2, 3]), sprintf("%.3f-%.3f", pi_sd[1, 3], pi_sd[2, 3]))
) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Reading" = reading, "omega^2 (E0)" = omega2_E0,
    "90% PI of median" = p50_PI, "90% PI of 90th percentile" = p90_PI
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  # Figure 4b at time 0: upper edge of the 90th-percentile band ~0.50.
  abs(pi_log[2, 3] / 0.50 - 1) < 0.25,
  pi_sd[2, 3] > 0.8
)
```

The log-CV reading reproduces the figure's predose bands; reading the CV as
omega would put the upper edge of the 90th-percentile band above 1.

# Healthy adults: simulation

```{r adult-sim}
N_ADULT <- 200L
pk_times <- sort(unique(c(seq(0, 3, by = 1 / 6), seq(3, 6, by = 1 / 3), seq(6, 8, by = 0.5), 12, 24, 48, 72)))
ev_adult <- make_adult_events(seq_len(N_ADULT), DOSE_ADULT_UG, pk_times) |>
  dplyr::mutate(treatment = "20 mg enalapril maleate")

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2025)
sim_adult <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_adult, ev_adult, keep = "treatment") |>
  as.data.frame()

typ_adult <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(mod_adult_typ, make_adult_events(1L, DOSE_ADULT_UG, pk_times)))

vpc_summary <- function(dat, var) {
  dat |>
    dplyr::group_by(time) |>
    dplyr::summarise(
      p10 = stats::quantile(.data[[var]], 0.10),
      p50 = stats::quantile(.data[[var]], 0.50),
      p90 = stats::quantile(.data[[var]], 0.90),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
}
```

## Figure 3b: enalaprilat VPC

```{r figure-3b}
vpc_pk <- vpc_summary(sim_adult, "sim")
ggplot(vpc_pk, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_line(data = typ_adult, aes(y = Cc), linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "Serum enalaprilat concentration (ug/L)",
    title = "Simulated enalaprilat, 200 healthy adults",
    caption = "Band: 10th-90th percentiles of simulated observations; solid: median; dashed: typical value.\nReplicates Figure 3b of Steichert 2025 (simulated percentiles only)."
  )
```

The `sim` column of the simulation output holds the simulated observation of
each sample's own endpoint. Because every observation row is placed on the
enalaprilat endpoint, `sim` is the enalaprilat observation including residual
error; the ratio observation is generated separately below.

The observed percentiles in Figure 3b peak at about 88 (90th), 38 (median) and
25 ug/L (10th) between 3 and 5 h and fall below 5 ug/L by 24 h. With nine
subjects the observed 90th percentile is close to the sample maximum; the
figure's 90% prediction interval for it spans about 50-96 ug/L at the peak, so
the population 90th percentile simulated below (about 66 ug/L) is consistent
with it.

```{r adult-pk-percentile-check}
pk_peak <- vpc_pk |>
  dplyr::filter(time >= 2, time <= 6) |>
  dplyr::summarise(p10 = max(p10), p50 = max(p50), p90 = max(p90))
pk_peak |> knitr::kable(digits = 1)
stopifnot(
  pk_peak$p50 > 30, pk_peak$p50 < 55,
  pk_peak$p90 > 50, pk_peak$p90 < 96,
  vpc_pk$p50[vpc_pk$time == 24] < 5
)
```

## Figure 4b: angiotensin II / angiotensin I ratio VPC

The PD residual error is proportional on the ratio, so a simulated observation
is `ratio * (1 + 0.41 * eps)`. The sampling grid is restricted to the PD
schedule (predose, 0.5, 1-8 and 24 h).

```{r figure-4b}
pd_times <- c(0, 0.5, 1:8, 24)
ev_adult_pd <- make_adult_events(seq_len(N_ADULT), DOSE_ADULT_UG, pd_times)
# Place the PD rows on the ratio endpoint (dvid = 2) so that sim is the
# simulated ratio observation.
ev_adult_pd$dvid[ev_adult_pd$evid == 0L] <- 2L

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2026)
sim_adult_pd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_adult, ev_adult_pd) |> as.data.frame()

vpc_pd <- vpc_summary(sim_adult_pd, "sim")
ggplot(vpc_pd, aes(time)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_point(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  labs(
    x = "Time (h)", y = "ANG II / ANG I ratio",
    title = "Simulated ANG II / ANG I ratio, 200 healthy adults",
    caption = "Band: 10th-90th percentiles of simulated observations; line: median.\nReplicates Figure 4b (and the adult part of Figure 5) of Steichert 2025."
  )
vpc_pd |> knitr::kable(digits = 3)

stopifnot(
  # Predose median near E0 (Figure 4b median band 0.03-0.085 at time 0).
  vpc_pd$p50[vpc_pd$time == 0] > 0.025, vpc_pd$p50[vpc_pd$time == 0] < 0.065,
  # The median falls by roughly half around 4-7 h and recovers by 24 h.
  min(vpc_pd$p50) < 0.6 * vpc_pd$p50[vpc_pd$time == 0],
  vpc_pd$p50[vpc_pd$time == 24] > 0.8 * vpc_pd$p50[vpc_pd$time == 0]
)
```

The typical ratio reaches its nadir after the enalaprilat peak (3.5 h) because
of the effect-compartment delay (`ke0` = 0.48 1/h, equilibration half-life
1.4 h), reproducing the clockwise hysteresis of Figure 2.

```{r hysteresis}
ggplot(typ_adult |> dplyr::filter(time <= 24), aes(Cc, ang2_ang1_ratio)) +
  geom_path() +
  geom_point(data = typ_adult |> dplyr::filter(time %in% c(0.5, 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 24)), aes(colour = factor(time))) +
  labs(
    x = "Serum enalaprilat concentration (ug/L)", y = "ANG II / ANG I ratio",
    colour = "Time (h)",
    title = "Typical-value hysteresis loop, healthy adult",
    caption = "Compare with the clockwise loop of one subject in Figure 2 of Steichert 2025."
  )
```

## PKNCA: enalaprilat after a single 20 mg enalapril maleate dose

The paper reports no NCA, only that the highest measured enalaprilat
concentration in the nine adults was 109 ug/L (Section 3.4). The NCA of the
simulated cohort is shown for reference.

```{r pknca-adult}
nca_conc <- sim_adult |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, Cc, treatment)
nca_dose <- ev_adult |>
  dplyr::filter(evid == 1L) |>
  dplyr::select(id, time, amt, treatment)

conc_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(nca_conc, Cc ~ time | treatment + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCA::PKNCAdose(nca_dose, amt ~ time | treatment + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = 0, end = Inf,
  cmax = TRUE, tmax = TRUE, aucinf.obs = TRUE, half.life = TRUE
)
nca_res <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))
nca_tbl <- as.data.frame(nca_res$result) |>
  dplyr::filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "tmax", "aucinf.obs", "half.life")) |>
  dplyr::group_by(treatment, PPTESTCD) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    median = stats::median(PPORRES, na.rm = TRUE),
    p05 = stats::quantile(PPORRES, 0.05, na.rm = TRUE),
    p95 = stats::quantile(PPORRES, 0.95, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
nca_tbl |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(median, p05, p95), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Treatment" = treatment, "NCA parameter" = PPTESTCD,
    "Median" = median, "5th percentile" = p05, "95th percentile" = p95
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

cmax_p95 <- nca_tbl$p95[nca_tbl$PPTESTCD == "cmax"]
stopifnot(cmax_p95 > 60, cmax_p95 < 160)
```

The simulated 95th percentile of Cmax brackets the highest measured value of
109 ug/L in nine subjects.

# Children with heart failure

## Figure 6b: ratio versus serum enalaprilat concentration

The paediatric model takes the serum enalaprilat concentration as the
covariate `CP_ENALAPRILAT_NGML`. Each virtual child below is observed once at
each concentration of a grid spanning the observed 0-18.3 ug/L.

```{r ped-sim}
N_PED <- 200L
conc_grid <- c(0, 0.5, 1, 1.6, 2.5, 3.5, 4.7, 6, 7.9, 10, 12, 14.9, 18)
ev_ped <- tidyr::expand_grid(id = seq_len(N_PED), CP_ENALAPRILAT_NGML = conc_grid) |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::mutate(time = seq_along(CP_ENALAPRILAT_NGML) - 1, evid = 0L, amt = 0) |>
  dplyr::ungroup()

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2027)
sim_ped <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ped, ev_ped, keep = "CP_ENALAPRILAT_NGML") |>
  as.data.frame()

vpc_ped <- sim_ped |>
  dplyr::group_by(CP_ENALAPRILAT_NGML) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    p10 = stats::quantile(sim, 0.10),
    p50 = stats::quantile(sim, 0.50),
    p90 = stats::quantile(sim, 0.90),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

typ_curve <- data.frame(conc = seq(0, 18, by = 0.1)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    children = 0.19 * (1 - conc / (conc + 1.19)),
    adults = 0.043 * (1 - conc^2.02 / (conc^2.02 + 30.01^2.02))
  )

ggplot(vpc_ped, aes(CP_ENALAPRILAT_NGML)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p10, ymax = p90), fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.3) +
  geom_line(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  geom_point(aes(y = p50), colour = "steelblue4") +
  labs(
    x = "Serum enalaprilat concentration (ug/L)", y = "ANG II / ANG I ratio",
    title = "Simulated ANG II / ANG I ratio, children with heart failure",
    caption = "Band: 10th-90th percentiles of simulated observations; line: median.\nReplicates Figure 6b of Steichert 2025."
  )
vpc_ped |> knitr::kable(digits = 3)
```

At zero concentration the model has no random effect (IIV on E0 was removed),
so the predose spread is the residual error alone:
`0.19 * (1 +/- 1.2816 * 0.37)` = 0.10-0.28 for the 10th and 90th percentiles,
matching the observed predose percentiles of Figure 6b (about 0.11, 0.19 and
0.27).

```{r ped-check}
typ_ped <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(rxode2::zeroRe(mod_ped), ev_ped |> dplyr::filter(id == 1L)))
stopifnot(
  # Typical value against its own closed form.
  isTRUE(all.equal(
    typ_ped$ang2_ang1_ratio,
    0.19 * (1 - conc_grid / (conc_grid + 1.19)),
    tolerance = 1e-8
  )),
  # Predose simulated percentiles against the residual-only expectation.
  abs(vpc_ped$p50[1] / 0.19 - 1) < 0.08,
  abs(vpc_ped$p90[1] / (0.19 * (1 + qnorm(0.9) * 0.37)) - 1) < 0.10
)
```

## Comparison with the adult concentration-response curve

The paediatric baseline ratio is higher (0.19 versus 0.043) and the IC50 much
lower (1.19 versus 30.01 ug/L) than in adults (Discussion). The plot shows the
typical curves as a fraction of baseline; the adult curve is plotted against
the effect-site concentration.

```{r compare-curves}
typ_curve |>
  dplyr::mutate(children = children / 0.19, adults = adults / 0.043) |>
  tidyr::pivot_longer(c(children, adults), names_to = "population", values_to = "frac") |>
  ggplot(aes(conc, frac, colour = population)) +
  geom_line() +
  labs(
    x = "Enalaprilat concentration (ug/L; effect site for adults)",
    y = "ANG II / ANG I ratio / baseline",
    colour = NULL,
    title = "Typical concentration-response, children vs adults"
  )
```

## Ratio change four hours after the first dose

Section 3.5 reports that in eight children (median age 0.22 years, range
0.07-0.58) the ratio fell by a median of 79.3% (range 21.4-92.7%) four hours
after a median first dose of 0.06 mg/kg enalapril maleate. The paper's
Conclusions suggest coupling the paediatric PD model to the group's paediatric
PK model; this section does that. Enalaprilat concentrations at 4 h are
simulated with `Steichert_2025_enalapril_enalaprilat_pediatric` (dose entered
as enalapril base), then passed to the PD model. The percentage change uses the
typical-value ratio before and after, so it reflects PK and IC50 variability
but not residual error.

```{r ped-first-dose}
mod_ped_pk <- readModelDb("Steichert_2025_enalapril_enalaprilat_pediatric")
set.seed(79)
N_FD <- 200L
cohort_fd <- data.frame(
  id = seq_len(N_FD),
  AGE = exp(stats::runif(N_FD, log(0.07), log(0.58)))
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    WT = pmin(pmax(4.8 * exp(stats::rnorm(N_FD, 0, 0.3)), 3.2), 13),
    CREAT = 23.37,
    SCORE_ROSS = 4
  )
ev_fd <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  cohort_fd |> dplyr::mutate(
    time = 0, evid = 1L, cmt = "depot", dvid = NA_integer_,
    amt = 0.06 * WT * 1000 * MW_ENALAPRIL / MW_ENALAPRIL_MALEATE
  ),
  cohort_fd |> dplyr::mutate(time = 4, evid = 0L, cmt = "central", dvid = 1L, amt = NA_real_)
) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

rxode2::rxSetSeed(2028)
pk_fd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ped_pk, ev_fd, keep = c("WT", "AGE")) |>
  as.data.frame()

# Pass the 4-h enalaprilat concentration (ug/L) to the PD model with IIV on
# IC50 and no residual error: predose (C = 0) and 4 h rows for each child.
ev_pd_fd <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  data.frame(id = pk_fd$id, time = 0, CP_ENALAPRILAT_NGML = 0),
  data.frame(id = pk_fd$id, time = 4, CP_ENALAPRILAT_NGML = pk_fd$Cc_enaat)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(2029)
pd_fd <- rxode2::rxSolve(mod_ped, ev_pd_fd, sigma = NA, keep = "CP_ENALAPRILAT_NGML") |>
  as.data.frame()

pct_change <- pd_fd |>
  dplyr::group_by(id) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    conc4 = CP_ENALAPRILAT_NGML[time == 4],
    decrease = 100 * (1 - ang2_ang1_ratio[time == 4] / ang2_ang1_ratio[time == 0]),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

data.frame(
  quantity = c("Enalaprilat at 4 h (ug/L)", "Ratio decrease at 4 h (%)"),
  median = c(stats::median(pct_change$conc4), stats::median(pct_change$decrease)),
  p10 = c(stats::quantile(pct_change$conc4, 0.1), stats::quantile(pct_change$decrease, 0.1)),
  p90 = c(stats::quantile(pct_change$conc4, 0.9), stats::quantile(pct_change$decrease, 0.9)),
  published = c(NA, 79.3)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(median, p10, p90), ~ signif(.x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Quantity" = quantity, "Simulated median" = median,
    "Simulated 10th percentile" = p10, "Simulated 90th percentile" = p90,
    "Published median (n = 8)" = published
  ) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  # The simulated median lies inside the observed range of the eight children.
  stats::median(pct_change$decrease) > 21.4,
  stats::median(pct_change$decrease) < 92.7
)
```

The chained prediction (a median decrease of about 69%) is close to the
observed median of 79.3% in eight children. The observed figure is a median of
eight noisy ratios, each carrying the 37% residual error twice, and the eight
children were younger than the PK model's reference subject, so an exact match
is not expected.

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Dose basis.** Doses are entered as enalapril free base. The paper does not
  state the basis; it is settled above against the population predictions of
  Figures 3a and 4a.
* **IIV scale.** Table 2 and Table 3 give IIV as CV%; the models use
  `omega^2 = log(1 + CV^2)`, the Monolix definition for log-normal parameters,
  and the predose VPC band of Figure 4b supports it over `omega = CV / 100`.
  The CL/F-V1/F covariance is `0.84 * omega_CL * omega_V1`.
* **Residual error forms.** The adult PK error is "combined additive and
  proportional" without a stated form; the Monolix default `combined1`
  (standard deviations summed, `a + b * f`) is used. The proportional errors
  are entered as reported (0.072, 0.41, 0.37); the predose percentiles of
  Figure 6b confirm that 0.37 is a standard deviation.
* **Transit absorption.** Monolix's `Mtt` / `Ktr` parameterisation is
  implemented with rxode2's `transit()`, with `n = Mtt * Ktr - 1` transit
  stages (6.75 for the typical subject). Because IIV acts on both `Mtt` and
  `Ktr`, `n` varies between subjects. `transit()` uses the most recent dose
  only, which is exact for the single-dose design of the adult study but
  approximate when doses overlap.
* **Censoring and LLOQ handling.** Enalaprilat values below the LLOQ were
  left-censored (M4) in the adult fit; paediatric angiotensin II values below
  the LLOQ were replaced by LLOQ/2 before forming the ratio. Neither affects
  simulation.
* **Validity window.** The adult PD data were limited to 0-24 h because the
  ratio overshot the baseline at 48 and 72 h in some subjects; the adult model
  does not describe that rebound.
* **Paediatric cohort for the first-dose check.** Age was drawn log-uniformly
  over 0.07-0.58 years and weight log-normally around the Table 1 median of
  4.8 kg (truncated to 3.2-13 kg); serum creatinine and Ross score were set to
  the PK model's reference values (23.37 umol/L, 4). The study's individual
  covariates are not published.
* **Figure values** quoted for comparison (PRED extremes in Figures 3a and 4a,
  VPC bands in Figures 3b, 4b and 6b) were read from the figures by the
  maintainers.
